newsitem.title: USA: GTS Duratek gets part of DOE contract.
newsitem.headline: GTS Duratek gets part of DOE contract.

text.p: GTS Duratek Inc said on Thursday it, along with other members of a team led by UK state-run British Nuclear Fuels, had won a contract for the Hanford Tank Waste cleanup at the Department of Energy's site in Washington state.
The total contract is estimated to be worth $2 billion to $4 billion over 11 years, it said. A company spokeswoman did not know how the contract would be divided among team members.
The company said in a statement the initial Phase 1-A was worth $27 million and would take 16 months to complete.
That phase starts with the design of a facility and initiation of a government permit process.
The group of companies involved includes BNFL Inc, the American subsidiary of British Nuclear Fuels; Bechtel National Inc, a unit of Bechtel Corp ; and Science Applications International Corp.
